class_ability_desc.arcane bond (ex or sp): At 1st level, wizards form a powerful bond with an object or a creature. This bond can take one of two forms: a familiar or a bonded object. A familiar is a magical pet that enhances the wizard's skills and senses and can aid him in magic, while a bonded object is an item a wizard can use to cast additional spells or to serve as a magical item. Once a wizard makes this choice, it is permanent and cannot be changed. Rules for bonded items are given below, while rules for familiars are at the end of this section. Wizards who select a bonded object begin play with one at no cost. Objects that are the subject of an arcane bond must fall into one of the following categories: amulet, ring, staff, wand, or weapon. These objects are always masterwork quality. Weapons acquired at 1st level are not made of any special material. If the object is an amulet or ring, it must be worn to have effect, while staves, wands, and weapons must be wielded. If a wizard attempts to cast a spell without his bonded object worn or in hand, he must make a concentration check or lose the spell. The DC for this check is equal to 20 + the spell's level. If the object is a ring or amulet, it occupies the ring or neck slot accordingly. A bonded object can be used once per day to cast any one spell that the wizard has in his spellbook and is capable of casting, even if the spell is not prepared. This spell is treated like any other spell cast by the wizard, including casting time, duration, and other effects dependent on the wizard's level. This spell cannot be modified by metamagic feats or other abilities. The bonded object cannot be used to cast spells from the wizard's opposition schools (see arcane school). A wizard can add additional magic abilities to his bonded object as if he has the required item creation feats and if he meets the level prerequisites of the feat. For example, a wizard with a bonded dagger must be at least 5th level to add magic abilities to the dagger (see the Craft Magic Arms and Armor feat in Feats). If the bonded object is a wand, it loses its wand abilities when its last charge is consumed, but it is not destroyed and it retains all of its bonded object properties and can be used to craft a new wand. The magic properties of a bonded object, including any magic abilities added to the object, only function for the wizard who owns it. If a bonded object's owner dies, or the item is replaced, the object reverts to being an ordinary masterwork item of the appropriate type. If a bonded object is damaged, it is restored to full hit points the next time the wizard prepares his spells. If the object of an arcane bond is lost or destroyed, it can be replaced after 1 week in a special ritual that costs 200 gp per wizard level plus the cost of the masterwork item. This ritual takes 8 hours to complete. Items replaced in this way do not possess any of the additional enchantments of the previous bonded item. A wizard can designate an existing magic item as his bonded item. This functions in the same way as replacing a lost or destroyed item except that the new magic item retains its abilities while gaining the benefits and drawbacks of becoming a bonded item.
class_ability_desc.arcane school: A wizard can choose to specialize in one school of magic, gaining additional spells and powers based on that school. This choice must be made at 1st level, and once made, it cannot be changed. A wizard that does not select a school receives the universalist school instead. A wizard that chooses to specialize in one school of magic must select two other schools as his opposition schools, representing knowledge sacrificed in one area of arcane lore to gain mastery in another. A wizard who prepares spells from his opposition schools must use two spell slots of that level to prepare the spell. For example, a wizard with evocation as an opposition school must expend two of his available 3rd-level spell slots to prepare a fireball . In addition, a specialist takes a -4 penalty on any skill checks made when crafting a magic item that has a spell from one of his opposition schools as a prerequisite. A universalist wizard can prepare spells from any school without restriction. Each arcane school gives the wizard a number of school powers. In addition, specialist wizards receive an additional spell slot of each spell level he can cast, from 1st on up. Each day, a wizard can prepare a spell from his specialty school in that slot. This spell must be in the wizard's spellbook. A wizard can select a spell modified by a metamagic feat to prepare in his school slot, but it uses up a higher-level spell slot. Wizards with the universalist school do not receive a school slot.
class_ability_desc.bonus feats: At 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th level, a wizard gains a bonus feat. At each such opportunity, he can choose a metamagic feat, an item creation feat, or Spell Mastery. The wizard must still meet all prerequisites for a bonus feat, including caster level minimums. These bonus feats are in addition to the feats that a character of any class gets from advancing levels. The wizard is not limited to the categories of item creation feats, metamagic feats, or Spell Mastery when choosing those feats.
class_ability_desc.bonus languages: A wizard may substitute Draconic for one of the bonus languages available to the character because of his race.
class_ability_desc.cantrips: Wizards can prepare a number of cantrips, or 0-level spells, each day, as noted on Table: Wizard under "Spells per Day."These spells are cast like any other spell, but they are not expended when cast and may be used again. A wizard can prepare a cantrip from a prohibited school, but it uses up two of his available slots (see below).
class_ability_desc.scribe scroll: At 1st level, a wizard gains Scribe Scroll as a bonus feat.
class_ability_desc.spellbooks: A wizard must study his spellbook each day to prepare his spells. He cannot prepare any spell not recorded in his spellbook, except for read magic, which all wizards can prepare from memory. A wizard begins play with a spellbook containing all 0-level wizard spells (except those from his prohibited schools, if any; see Arcane Schools) plus three 1st-level spells of his choice. The wizard also selects a number of additional 1st-level spells equal to his Intelligence modifier to add to the spellbook. At each new wizard level, he gains two new spells of any spell level or levels that he can cast (based on his new wizard level) for his spellbook. At any time, a wizard can also add spells found in other wizards' spellbooks to his own (see Magic). Alternate Capstones
class_ability_desc.spells: A wizard casts arcane spells drawn from the sorcerer/wizard spell list presented in Spell Lists. A wizard must choose and prepare his spells ahead of time. To learn, prepare, or cast a spell, the wizard must have an Intelligence score equal to at least 10 + the spell level. The Difficulty Class for a saving throw against a wizard's spell is 10 + the spell level + the wizard's Intelligence modifier. A wizard can cast only a certain number of spells of each spell level per day. His base daily spell allotment is given on Table: Wizard. In addition, he receives bonus spells per day if he has a high Intelligence score (see Table: Ability Modifiers and Bonus Spells). A wizard may know any number of spells. He must choose and prepare his spells ahead of time by getting 8 hours of sleep and spending 1 hour studying his spellbook. While studying, the wizard decides which spells to prepare.

Scroll Scholar.diligent student (ex): At 1st level, a scroll scholar chooses one Knowledge skill. This becomes a class skill if it is not already one. The scroll scholar adds half her class level to all Knowledge checks of this type (minimum 1). At 5th level and every five levels thereafter, a scroll scholar chooses 1 additional Knowledge skill to receive this bonus. For clerics, this ability replaces one of the 1st-level granted powers from her domains-the character gets to choose which of her two 1st-level granted powers it replaces. For wizards, this ability replaces diviner's fortune (if a diviner) or hand of the apprentice (if a universalist).
Scroll Scholar.flash of insight (su): At 10th level, once per day, a scroll scholar can gain a +5 bonus on a single attack roll, caster level check, or saving throw as an immediate action. This decision must be made before the results of the roll are known, but can be made after the die is rolled. This ability can be used twice per day at 15th level, and 3 times per day at 20th level. This ability replaces the normal addition of a new 4th-level spell slot to the character's spells per day- from this point on, the cleric or wizard has one fewer 4thlevel spell slot than other clerics or wizards.
Scroll Scholar.secrets revealed (sp): At 5th level, a scroll scholar gains the ability to cast comprehend languages and identify as spelllike abilities. Her caster level is equal to her character level in whatever class she took the scroll scholar archetype for. She can cast these spells once per day each at 5th level, twice per day each at 7th level, and three times per day each at 9th level. At 11th level, one of these spell-like abilities (scholar's choice) becomes a constant spell-like ability, and at 13th level, the second one becomes a constant spell-like ability. If the scholar is a cleric, this ability replaces the increase to her channel energy damage normally gained at 5th level-her channel energy damage increases to 3d6 at 7th level instead, and for the rest of her career as a cleric lags 1d6 behind normal. If the scholar is a wizard, this ability replaces her bonus feat for 5th level.
Scroll Scholar.source: Pathfinder Society Field Guide pg. 26 A scroll scholar values knowledge and learning as much as her other abilities, trading a portion of her potential in her chosen class for greater breadth of skill at deciphering old texts, piecing together strange fragments of esoteric lore, and deciphering the hidden qualities of strange and unusual magical items. The scroll scholar archetype can be taken by either clerics or wizards-they give up different class abilities for the new abilities granted by this archetype. A wizard must either be a universalist wizard or a diviner wizard in order to take this archetype-other types of school specializations are not suited to this archetype's focus. A scroll scholar has the following class features.

Aquadynamic.description: This sleek and mobile armor is magically streamlined to assist in swimming rather than making swimming more difficult, granting the wearer a +5 competence bonus on Swim checks for aquadynamic armor, a +10 competence bonus on Swim checks for improved aquadynamic armor, and a +15 competence bonus on Swim checks for greater aquadynamic armor.

contextNotes.text: Mental Focus: +[[2]] enhancement on concentration checks; an occultist may spend [[1]] hour attuning [[1]]/day to gain [[1]] extra point of mental focus (lost if the armor is removed).

Mental Focus.description: Armor enhanced with the mental focus special ability grants its wearer a +2 enhancement bonus on concentration checks. If the wearer has the mental focus OA occultist class feature, once per day he can also spend 1 hour attuning himself to the armor to gain 1 additional point of mental focus . This point of mental focus is lost if the armor is removed. The mental focus special ability can be applied only to medium armor.

belts.description: this belt's golden buckle depicts a bear's head. The belt grants the wearer an enhancement bonus to constitution of +2, +4, or +6. Treat this as a temporary ability bonus for the first 24 hours the belt is worn.

body.description: this coarse hempen robe seems made from a single strand of twine. The wearer can draw up to 30 feet of twine or up to 10 feet of hemp rope per round from the robe without harming it. As an immediate action, the wearer can draw up to 150 feet of twine or 50 feet of rope from the robe, but this gives the robe the broken condition and suppresses its powers until it is repaired. Twine or rope drawn from the robe remains connected until cut or torn, but is treated as common material rather than part of a magic item. Pieces removed become normal twine or rope.

chest.description: this leather vest is fitted with a number of pockets that are useful for storing the ingredients necessary for alchemical tinkering.  the main ability of this vest, however, is to lessen the debilitating effects of an alchemist's mutagen. While under the effect of any type of mutagen, the wearer takes no penalty to mental ability scores from that mutagen.

eyes.description: this lens, mounted in a round silver frame, fits snugly in the eye orbit of any medium or small user. Three times per day on command, the monocle allows the user to read magical inscriptions (including scrolls) as if affected by read magic once per day, by speaking a second command word, the user can activate a 1stlevel spell from a scroll even if she doesn't have the spell on her class list or meet the other requirements. Activating a scroll with the monocle is a full-round action (or the spell's casting time, whichever is longer).

hands.description: the wearer of these simple gloves can speak a command word create a glowing disembodied hand. As a swift action, the wearer can have the hand assist him with a task as if using the aid another action.  the hand uses the wearer's base attack bonus or skill ranks when making the check to see if aid another is successful (it does not gain the benefit of the wearer's ability scores or other bonuses). The hand remains until it has attempted one action or until 1 minute passes, whichever comes first, at which time the gloves become nonmagical.

headband.description: this intricate gold headband is decorated with several small blue and deep purple gemstones. The headband grants the wearer an enhancement bonus to intelligence of +2, +4, or +6. Treat this as a temporary ability bonus for the first 24 hours the headband is worn. A headband of vast intelligence has one skill associated with it per +2 bonus it grants. After being worn for 24 hours, the headband grants a number of skill ranks in those skills equal to the wearer's total hit dice. These ranks do not stack with the ranks a creature already possesses.  these skills are chosen when the headband is created. If no skill is listed, the headband is assumed to grant skill ranks in randomly determined knowledge skills.

neck.description: this amulet, usually containing some type of magically preserved monster hide or other natural armorsuch as bone, horn, carapace, or beast scales toughens the wearer's body and flesh,  giving him an enhancement bonus to his natural armor from +1 to +5,  depending on the kind of amulet.

rings.description: This ring offers continual magical protection in the form of a deflection bonus of +1 to +5 to AC.

shoulders.description: flecks of silver or steel are often sown amid the fabric of these magical cloaks. This garment offers magical protection in the form of a +1 to +5 resistance bonus on all saving throws (fortitude, reflex, and will).

wrist.description: these translucent cloth tubes easily fit over their wearer's arms. The wearer of these sleeves can, when she slips them on, choose to transform the appearance of her current garments into any other nonmagical set of clothing. These new clothes fit her perfectly and are always clean and mended unless she specifically designates otherwise. When she removes the sleeves, her clothes revert to their original form.

contextNotes.text: +2 on Perception checks while in a primarily underground or mountainous environment (+4 with 10+ ranks in Knowledge (dungeoneering)).

City Slicker.description: You suffer from a lack of experience in the wilds. You take a -2 penalty on Survival and Handle Animal checks.

contextNotes.text: Elemental Vulnerability: you take +[[50]]% damage from your chosen energy type.

Elemental Vulnerability.description: One energy type (chosen when this flaw is gained: fire, cold, electricity, or acid) ravages you. You take 50% more damage from that energy type.

contextNotes.text: Shattered Psyche: -[[2]] on Intelligence-based skill checks.
Shattered Psyche: -[[2]] on Wisdom-based skill checks.

Shattered Psyche.description: Your mind is crowded with dozens of voices, fragmented snippets of your past lives. You take a -2 penalty on all Intelligence-based skill checks, Wisdom-based skill checks, and concentration checks.

formatted_bio:
Pauline Dupont
- Alignment: Neutral Good
- Deity: Ragathiel
- Race: Human
- Class: Level 15 Wizard
- Archetype: Magic Battlefield Controller
- Tactics: Never races the enemy's damage -- changes the terms instead: a wall splits their line, a pit deletes a flanker, fog blinds the archers. Each round it removes options until the survivors stand exactly where its party wants them.
- Stat Focus: Int
- Homeland: Tal-falko

Vocation
- Profession: Charm-Peddler (rank 15)
- Profession: Medusa Hunter (rank 6)
- Profession: Stoneshaper (rank 1)
- Profession: Book Seller (rank 1)
- Profession: Sea Urchin Harvester (rank 7)
- Known for: Locks
- Training: An average trainer who taught them Dragoncrafting, Antagonize
- Training: An excellent trainer who taught them Flash of Insight, Burning Spell, Cursed Item Detection
- Training: An excellent trainer who taught them Piercing Spell, Blade of Terror, Mind Trick
- Training: An excellent trainer who taught them Totem Spirit, Intensified Spell, Selective Spell

Family
- Loving Mother
- Absent Father
- Raised In A Wealthy Household
- 1 Older Sister
- 3 Younger Sisters

Personality
- Personality: Enthusiastic, Agreeable, Goal-oriented, Judicious, Gregarious
- Mannerisms: Taps pencil, Rub hands together, Bursts into laughter, Crouches
- Flaws: City Slicker, Shattered Psyche, Elemental Vulnerability

Appearance
- Hair: Wavy Black
- Eyes: Blue
- Build: Flawless Skin

homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Alertness: You often notice things that others might miss
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Animal Affinity: You are skilled at working with animals and mounts
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Antagonize: Whether with biting remarks or hurtful words, you are adept at making creatures angry with you
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Blade of Terror: You have learned to blend the fearsome arts of the dread with your mind blade. you may use your mind blade to deliver your terrors as if you had used your devastating touch, and you may add half your soulknife level (rounded down) to your dread level to determine saving throws for your terrors. additionally, anytime you successfully use a fear effect (either through a terror or a manifested power) you may regain your psychic strike as a free action once per round.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Burning Spell: You cause creatures to take extra damage when you affect them with a spell that has the acid or fire descriptor
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Cursed Item Detection: Your arcane prowess is so great that even cursed items fail to befuddle you
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Deceitful: You are skilled at deceiving others, both with the spoken word and with physical disguises
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Demonologist: You have immersed yourself deeply in studies of the nature of the Abyss and its inhabitants
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Dragoncrafting: You have the ability to create rare and valuable items from the bodies of fallen true dragons
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Extra Cantrips Or Orisons: You are a master of minor spells
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Flash of Insight: Discipline Sleeping Goddess (Boost); Level 1 Initiation Action 1 swift action Range 30 ft. Target One or two allies (see text) Duration Instantaneous You turn a sudden burst of inspiration into strength for your allies, sharing your power to give them an edge in battle and help them shrug of their wounds. You can activate this boost after making a successful attack or combat maneuver check. One ally within 30 feet gains another saving throw against a non-instantaneous effect that allows a saving throw affecting them. This saving throw has the same DC as the original save. If your ally succeeds, the effect ends. The ally does not suffer any additional effects for failing the save (such as a poisons damage). You cannot grant an ally more than one additional save against a given effect. Augment You can augment this maneuver in one or more of the following ways
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Improved Initiative: Your quick ref lexes allow you to react rapidly to danger
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Intensified Spell: Your spells can go beyond several normal limitations
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Magical Aptitude: You are skilled at spellcasting and using magic items
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Mind Trick: This is not the one you are looking for. Special You can take this feat multiple times. Its effects do not stack; you must select a different class skill each time you take this feat. select 1 class skill which uses dexterity as its associated ability score, such as sleight of hand or stealth. you can use charisma as its associated ability score instead (this allows you to ignore armor check penalty for the chosen skill). in addition, when you use the aid another action to provide a bonus to another creature attempting a check with the selected skill, increase that bonus by your charisma modifier.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Multi Talented: Your profession rank cap increases by 10.
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Noble Scion: You are a member of a proud noble family, whether or not you remain in good standing with your family
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Persuasive: You are skilled at swaying attitudes and intimidating others into your way of thinking
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Piercing Spell: Your studies have helped you develop methods to overcome spell resistance
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Scholar: You have graduated from one of the many colleges, universities, and specialty schools of higher learning scattered throughout the Inner Sea region
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Selective Spell: Your allies need not fear friendly fire
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Self-Sufficient: You know how to get along in the wild and how to effectively treat wounds
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Spell Focus: Choose a school of magic Any spells you cast of that school are more difficult to resist
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Spell Penetration: Your spells break through spell resistance more easily than most
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Stone Read: Even the faint movement and vibrations of stone can alert you to trouble
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.Totem Spirit: You are mystically tied to your tribe's sacred totem
homebrew_feat_desc_dict.True Calling: Your natural Profession rank cap rises to 15 in one qualifying profession.

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Charm-Peddler) - rank 15/15. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Use Magic Device, Sense Motive, Perception, Profession.

Evil Eye (Ex)

Wizard can fix a victim with a baleful stare laden with petty malice. Three times per day as a standard action, one creature within 30 feet that Wizard can see takes a -2 penalty on saving throws against fear for 1 minute (no save to resist this minor curse).

Graveyard Manners (Ex)

Long nights spent in crypts and at deathbeds have inured Wizard to the company of corpses. Grants a +2 competence bonus on Heal checks to treat the dying and a +2 morale bonus on saving throws against fear and disease.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Charm-Peddler)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Charm-Peddler) - rank 15/15.

Cultist's Cant (Ex)

Schooled in whispered creeds and secret signs, Wizard sways the faithful and the fearful alike. Grants a +2 competence bonus on Intimidate checks and a +2 competence bonus on Bluff checks made to spread rumor or conceal heresy.

Petty Hex (Su)

Wizard knows one minor witch's hex (such as a sleep curse, a fortune jinx, or a misfortune touch). They may use it at will as a standard action; the save DC is 10 + half their character level + their Charisma modifier, and a target that saves is immune to that hex for 24 hours.

Cantrips of the Coven (Sp)

Wizard can cast bleed, detect magic, touch of fatigue, and putrefy food and drink at will as spell-like abilities (caster level equal to their character level).
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 15: (Charm-Peddler)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Medusa Hunter) - rank 6/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Knowledge (local), Craft.

Sea Legs (Ex)

Long voyages have given you flawless balance aboard a pitching deck. You gain a +2 competence bonus on Swim checks and a +2 competence bonus on Acrobatics checks made to keep your balance on unstable or moving surfaces, and you are never sickened by motion or seasickness.

Beast Soother (Ex)

A calm word and a steady hand settle skittish animals. You gain a +2 competence bonus on Handle Animal checks, and you may attempt to influence the attitude of an animal as a Diplomacy check using your Handle Animal modifier.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Medusa Hunter)

profession_ability_items.description:
Profession (Sea Urchin Harvester) - rank 7/10. Associate skills (ranks 1/4/7/10): Appraise, Sleight of Hand, Perception.

Shifty Eyes (Ex)

Always watching for marks and witnesses, the Wizard notices the small things others miss. They gain a +2 competence bonus on Perception checks.

Light Fingers (Ex)

A lifetime of palming coins and lifting purses makes petty theft second nature. The Wizard gains a +2 circumstance bonus on Sleight of Hand checks.
profession_ability_items.name: Profession Rank 5: (Sea Urchin Harvester)

rank5_abilities.desc: A lifetime of palming coins and lifting purses makes petty theft second nature. The Wizard gains a +2 circumstance bonus on Sleight of Hand checks.
rank5_abilities.name: Light Fingers (Ex)

selected_traits_desc.description: Whenever you channel positive energy to heal living creatures, affected targets gain a +2 profane bonus to CMD to resist bull rush, reposition, and trip combat maneuvers. Alternately, if you channel negative energy to harm living creatures, affected targets take a –2 penalty to CMD against such combat maneuvers. This effect lasts 1 round.
selected_traits_desc.name: Channel the Earth (Plane of Earth)

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on Climb checks, and Climb becomes a class skill for you.
selected_traits_desc.name: Seasoned Climber

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +1 trait bonus on Heal checks, and Heal is always a class skill for you.
selected_traits_desc.name: Caretaker

selected_traits_desc.description: The Sense Motive DC needed for a city guard, a politician, or other governmental functionary in a large town or larger settlement to gain a hunch about your trustworthiness is 25 (instead of 20). On a failed check, you're seen as trustworthy regardless of the situation.
selected_traits_desc.name: Evident Supporter

selected_traits_desc.description: Whenever you cast a spell from the transmutation school, its effects manifest at +1 caster level. Additionally, select one of the following transmutation spells: bear's endurance, bull's strength, cat's grace, eagle's splendor, fox's cunning, or owl's wisdom. Once per day when you cast that spell, its duration is doubled. A spell affected by this trait cannot be modified further by the Extend Spell metamagic feat or similar abilities.
selected_traits_desc.name: Transmuter

selected_traits_desc.description: You gain a +4 trait bonus on Handle Animal checks related to large creatures such as mammoths, mastodons, woolly rhinoceroses, and other megafauna.
selected_traits_desc.name: Mammoth Master

selected_traits_desc.description: Select one of the following skills: Disable Device or Sleight of Hand. You gain a +1 trait bonus on that skill, and it is always a class skill for you.
selected_traits_desc.name: Vagabond Child

selected_traits_desc.description: Pick one of the three categories of saving throw. You gain a +1 trait bonus on all saving throws of that type.
selected_traits_desc.name: Into Enemy Territory

unlock.10: Your swim speed equals your base speed in water of DC 15 or lower, and 10 feet in other water.
unlock.15: You ignore the penalties for using slashing or bludgeoning weapons underwater, as freedom of movement.
unlock.20: Your swim speed equals your base speed in all water, and you gain a +8 racial bonus on Swim checks with both hands free.
unlock.5: You gain a swim speed of 10 feet in water with a Swim DC of 15 or lower.

skill_unlock.unlock_html:
Swim

5 Ranks: You gain a swim speed of 10 feet in water with a Swim DC of 15 or lower.

10 Ranks: Your swim speed equals your base speed in water of DC 15 or lower, and 10 feet in other water.

15 Ranks: You ignore the penalties for using slashing or bludgeoning weapons underwater, as freedom of movement.

20 Ranks: Your swim speed equals your base speed in all water, and you gain a +8 racial bonus on Swim checks with both hands free.

Flame Arrow.name: Flame Arrow: turns ammunition such as arrows, bolts, shuriken, and sling stones into fiery projectiles that deal extra fire damage on a hit and can ignite flammable objects (but not creatures). Duration [[10]] min./level.

Form of the Dragon III.name: Form of the Dragon III: as form of the dragon II, but you take the form of a Huge chromatic or metallic dragon, gaining +[[10]] size Strength, +[[8]] size Constitution, +[[8]] natural armor, fly [[120]] feet (poor), blindsense [[60]] feet, darkvision [[120]] feet, a breath weapon, DR [[10]]/magic, frightful presence (DC = this spell's DC), and immunity to one element. Natural attacks are one bite ([[2d8]]), two claws ([[2d6]]), two wings ([[1d8]]), and one tail slap ([[2d6]]). The breath weapon recharges after [[1d4]] rounds between uses and allows a Reflex save for half breath damage; lines become [[100]]-foot lines and cones become [[50]]-foot cones. Duration [[1]] minute/level.

Form of the Exotic Dragon II.name: Form of the Exotic Dragon II: as form of the exotic dragon I, but you take the form of a Large imperial or primal dragon, gaining +[[6]] size Strength, +[[4]] size Constitution, +[[6]] natural armor, fly [[90]] feet (poor), darkvision [[60]] feet, a breath weapon, DR [[5]]/magic, and resistance to one form of energy or another bonus. Natural attacks are one bite ([[2d6]]), two claws ([[1d8]]), a tail slap ([[1d8]]), and either a gore ([[2d6]]) for an imperial dragon or two wings ([[1d6]]) for a primal dragon. The breath weapon allows a Reflex save to halve the breath damage; lines become [[80]]-foot lines and cones become [[40]]-foot cones. Duration [[1]] minute/level.

riders: Range: [[400 + 40*@spells.primary.cl.total]] ft; Save: Will DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates; target takes a -[[5]] penalty on all skill checks and ability checks to investigate, pursue, or otherwise advance its goals in relation to the designated subject, and typically does not attempt such checks if they can be avoided; if the designated activity would be harmful for the target to refrain from doing (such as eating, sleeping, or holding its breath underwater), the target gains a +[[5]] bonus on the saving throw or check required by its inaction, and receives a new saving throw with the same +[[5]] bonus immediately after to negate this spell; this bonus increases by [[1]] for each subsequent check required by the same condition; the spell immediately ends if you directly interact with the target, such as by engaging it in combat or targeting it with another spell or effect

Range: [[0]] ft; cast just before casting another spell; cutting your hand deals [[1d6]] damage to you and transforms your blood into one material component of your choice required by the second spell cast that round; components worth more than [[1]] gp cost an additional [[1]] point of Strength damage, plus a further [[1]] point for every full [[500]] gp of the component's value (a component worth [[500]]-[[999]] gp costs [[2]] points total, [[1]],[[000]]-[[1]],[[499]] gp costs [[3]] points total, and so on); magic items cannot be created with blood money; components created this way transform back into blood at the end of the round if not used as a material component; spellcasters without blood cannot cast blood money, and casters immune to Strength damage cannot use it to create valuable material components

Range: [[25 + 5*floor(@spells.primary.cl.total/2)]] ft; Save: Will DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates; humanoid target treats the caster as a trusted friend and ally (attitude: friendly) for [[@spells.primary.cl.total]] hours; target gains a +[[5]] bonus on its save if it is currently being threatened or attacked by the caster or its allies; caster may give the target orders, but must win an opposed Charisma check to convince it to do anything it wouldn't ordinarily do (no retries); affected creature never obeys suicidal or obviously harmful orders, though it might be convinced something very dangerous is worth doing; any act by the caster or its apparent allies that threatens the charmed creature breaks the spell; caster must speak the target's language to communicate commands or be skilled at pantomime; spell resistance: yes

Range: touch; Save: Fortitude DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates; target is staggered and moves at half its normal speed (rounded down to the next [[5]]-foot increment) for [[@spells.primary.cl.total]] rounds; target can hold its breath for twice as long as normal during this time; spell resistance: yes

Range: [[25 + 5*floor(@spells.primary.cl.total/2)]] ft; Save: Will DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates; targets only creatures with the ooze type, creatures with the amorphous special ability, and non-bipedal creatures with a special association with the Outer Gods, no two of which may be more than [[30]] ft. apart; draws the targets' attention to you as per the fascinate bardic performance ability; it affects mindless creatures despite the mindless quality normally granting immunity to mind-affecting effects, though it does not ignore any other immunity to mind-affecting effects a creature might have; you do not need to maintain the effect each round, as the music continues for the spell's duration; creatures fascinated by this spell become immune to any other casting of it for [[24]] hours after the spell ends, and the spell ends for all targets if the fascination breaks on any of them for any reason (such as an attack); if you have the bardic performance class feature and the fascinate bardic performance, you can choose to use the spell's save DC or a DC equal to [[10]] plus half your levels in the class that grants bardic performance plus your Charisma modifier, whichever is higher; if you use the latter DC, each round of the melody costs [[1]] round of bardic performance and counts as an active performance for determining how many performances you can have active; each time you cast this spell you take [[1d4]] Wisdom damage, or [[2d6]] sanity damage instead if your campaign uses the sanity system; spell resistance: yes

Cost: [[150]] gp material component (powdered turquoise); Range: [[25 + 5*floor(@spells.primary.cl.total/2)]] ft; Save: Will DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates; the target's malice is directed at a second creature designated by you at the time of casting; the target subtly attempts to slander, abuse, and plot against that individual, remaining within its financial and ethical means while pushed to the limit of what it would do to a hated foe; each day, the target takes [[2]] Wisdom damage as the spite dominates its thoughts, which can only be alleviated by the target performing a spiteful act against the designated individual; when the spell ends, the target remembers its spiteful behavior but not the motivation behind it; spell resistance: yes

Cost: [[15]] gp material component (dose of pesh); Range: touch; Save: Will DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates; target gains a +[[2]] enhancement bonus to Strength; as a free action once per round, the target can increase the enhancement bonus by [[2]] for [[1]] round, taking [[1d6]] nonlethal damage and reducing the spell's duration by [[1]] additional round; for every [[5]] caster levels the caster has, the target can increase the bonus by an additional [[2]] (taking an additional [[1d6]] nonlethal damage and reducing the duration by [[1]] additional round per increase), to a maximum enhancement bonus of +[[10]] and [[4d6]] nonlethal damage at caster level [[15]]th; the target cannot spend more rounds than remain in the duration; when the spell ends, the target becomes fatigued; spell resistance: yes

Range: [[25 + 5*floor(@spells.primary.cl.total/2)]] ft; Save: Will DC [[ 10 + @slvl + @castMod ]] negates (see below); if the target fails its save, a glowing rune identifying its most susceptible deadly sin appears on its body (usually the brow) and it is overwhelmed with an inability to repress urges to indulge that sin; each round at the start of its turn, the target must attempt a new Will save against the spell's DC: if it succeeds, it is sickened for that round by the distractions of its sin; if it fails, it is sickened and staggered as it spends part of its action wallowing in its sin; lasts up to [[@spells.primary.cl.total]] rounds; spell resistance: yes
